tldr: MedRAX is the first versatile AI agent framework that dynamically integrates multiple specialized CXR analysis tools with multimodal LLMs via a ReAct reasoning loop to address complex medical queries without requiring additional training, achieving state-of-the-art performance on the proposed ChestAgentBench benchmark.
contributions: MedRAX, a specialized AI agent framework integrating multiple CXR analysis tools without additional training, dynamically orchestrating specialized components for complex medical queries

ChestAgentBench, a benchmark of 2,500 six-choice complex medical queries across 7 categories (detection, classification, localization, comparison, relationship, characterization, diagnosis), built from 675 expert-curated clinical cases from Eurorad
Demonstration that MedRAX outperforms both general-purpose and biomedical specialist models in complex reasoning tasks
Development of a user-friendly Gradio-based interface supporting multi-turn interactions and transparent tool execution
methods: MedRAX uses GPT-4o with vision as its backbone LLM driving a ReAct (Reasoning and Acting) loop, iteratively observing queries, generating thoughts, and executing tools. It integrates specialized models: CheXagent and LLaVA-Med for visual question answering, MedSAM and PSPNet for segmentation, Maira-2 for grounding, a SwinV2 Transformer with BERT decoder for report generation, TorchXRayVision DenseNet-121 for disease classification across 18 pathology classes, and RoentGen for CXR generation. The framework is built on LangChain and LangGraph, supports parallel tool execution, caches outputs in memory to avoid redundancy, and allows flexible deployment from local to cloud. ChestAgentBench questions were generated by prompting GPT-4o to analyze 675 Eurorad clinical cases, followed by automated quality verification for structural consistency and explicit grounding.
results: MedRAX achieves state-of-the-art performance compared to both open-source and proprietary models on ChestAgentBench, including comparisons against GPT-4o, Llama-3.2-90B Vision, CheXagent, LLaVA-Med, RadFM, MAIRA-1, LLaVA-Rad, and Med-PaLM M 84B. The paper also evaluates on CheXbench (VQA and fine-grained image-text reasoning subsets) and mentions MIMIC-CXR Radiography evaluation, though specific numerical results are cut off from the provided text. Models are evaluated using accuracy as the metric, with regex-based answer extraction and up to three retries for unclear responses.
limitations: Existing foundation multimodal models face hallucinations and inconsistencies in reasoning, particularly where medical accuracy is paramount
Benchmark questions were generated and verified using GPT-4o, introducing potential bias or ungrounded answers (though automated quality checks removed some)
Questions with ungrounded answers or missing information were removed during quality checks, potentially limiting benchmark coverage
The truncated text prevents full reporting of all numerical results across benchmarks
